historical_claims.anchor: The spice can be found in one place alone, the desert planet Arrakis, also called Dune.
Yueh disables the Atreides defenses, allowing Harkonnen forces and the emperor's disguised Sardaukar troops to attack.
Her unborn daughter receives awareness while still in the womb, an experience for which the Bene Gesserit have dire warnings.
Gurney, believing Jessica betrayed the duke, turns on her.
The Sardaukar discover that their reputation does not make them invincible.
Paul demands a marriage to the emperor's daughter, Princess Irulan, as the political instrument that will place him on the imperial throne.

editorial_scope: Complete story-first orientation to Herbert's first novel, including the Fremen, spice, prescience, final battle and troubled ending.
reference_caveat: Original interpretive prose. Literature sources with protected full text are cited bibliographically, not reproduced; linked study guides or scholarly abstracts do not replace the primary text. Interpretive claims are presented as analysis, not documentary fact.

work.note: Existing survey chapter label '1965 · Dune' supplies the work's publication year; bibliography identifies the work. This dates publication, not its fictional setting or the lecture's creation.

description: Retells Herbert’s Dune through House Atreides’ fall, Paul and Jessica’s refuge among the Fremen, the struggle over spice and Arrakis’s ecology, and Paul’s ascent to the imperial throne. Follows planted prophecy, prescience, and the threatened religious war that complicate his apparent victory.
